summary:
BHOOMI is an interactive agricultural research and planning platform designed to support climate-resilient farming. As global warming changes rainfall patterns, temperatures, and growing conditions, farmers and agricultural researchers face increasing uncertainty in selecting suitable crops and managing resources.

BHOOMI integrates NASA POWER climate observations, MODIS vegetation data, and satellite-based soil moisture and precipitation map layers into a unified platform. Users can explore geographical locations, examine environmental conditions, draw farmland boundaries, and experiment with different crops, irrigation methods, and climate scenarios.

The platform also allows users to compare illustrative farming outcomes, save experiments, and generate preliminary action plans. While its environmental observations come from NASA datasets, its farming simulations are currently exploratory and require scientific validation.

Designed primarily for agricultural researchers, BHOOMI aims to bridge the gap between Earth observation data and practical farming decisions. By helping researchers investigate potential agricultural strategies, the platform seeks to support better-informed recommendations for farmers and contribute to a more sustainable, climate-resilient agricultural future.
details:
BHOOMI is an interactive agricultural research and planning platform that integrates NASA Earth observation data with geospatial visualization and farming simulations. It helps agricultural researchers analyze environmental conditions and explore farming strategies under changing climate conditions.

The platform uses NASA POWER for temperature, rainfall, humidity, and modeled soil wetness, MODIS for vegetation monitoring, and NASA GIBS for satellite-based environmental map layers. Users can select locations, draw farmland boundaries, analyze historical data, simulate different farming conditions, compare illustrative outcomes, and save experiments.

BHOOMI was developed using React, JavaScript, Vite, Python, FastAPI, MapLibre, Leaflet, and Recharts. Its innovation lies in combining multiple NASA datasets with interactive agricultural planning tools in one accessible platform.

The project aims to help researchers investigate climate-resilient farming strategies that could eventually benefit farmers through scientifically validated recommendations. Currently, simulation results are illustrative rather than validated predictions. Future development will focus on AI-assisted crop recommendations, improved simulation accuracy, and crop rotation analysis.
